Art Bus On Hope is a little free pottery library that has quickly expanded to all sorts of art forms! We created it to share our extra handmade pottery from the studio and our personal collection as a gift to our neighbors to enjoy, but we have had so many amazing artists want to contribute as well. Everything is created with love to share beauty, creativity, and kindness in our community. Art is for everyone! summary: Instagram: @whithamiltonart I began a sidewalk art gallery using my basement’s front windows to exhibit oil paintings I have created
detail:
Instagram: @whithamiltonart

I began a sidewalk art gallery using my basement’s front windows to exhibit oil paintings I have created. It began during the Pandemic and I began to decorate the yard and made a permanent earth temple out of organic found material. The yard decorations change every 6 weeks based on various holidays. This year we sculpted a 7 foot Krampus from scraps of wood and leather.

Image Description (optional)

There are two large figurative oil paintings in the basement windows illuminated with lights. Depending on the holiday the yard is decorated with whimsical sculptures and lights. Every Halloween and Christmas we highlight a different country’s ancient folklore

name: Belleville FLAG
summary: IG: @Belleville_FLAG Inspired by CR Boothe’s Highland Park FLAG, also in Roanoke, VA the Belleville FLAG was designed and built in the fall of 2025
detail:
IG: @Belleville_FLAG

Inspired by CR Boothe’s Highland Park FLAG, also in Roanoke, VA the Belleville FLAG was designed and built in the fall of 2025. My dad was an artist, I have always appreciated art, and as an adult recently started playing around with watercolor. I find painting is almost like meditation, it helps me clear my head and focus on the present. I love to happen upon little surprises on a neighborhood walk. A friend who helped me build this FLAG filled a tiny tree hole with a tiny door up the street — see if you can find it when you stop by this FLAG!) I love creating and I have lots of creative friends who do too. Stop by, have a look at the gallery, take a piece that you love home to enjoy, or regift, drop off your own art for people to enjoy.

We have no sidewalks on our street, but visitors are welcome to walk in or park in the gravel to check it out.

The Lamasco Microgallery was established in 2023 as a grassroots initiative to serve the Lamasco neighborhood as the primary audience and greater Evansville as the secondary. The microgallery aims to create a less restrictive environment where artists and viewers are emancipated from a traditional museum or gallery perceptions and confinements. The dimensions of the exhibition space are 20.75″L × 10″H × 5.5″W, and is used to exhibit local, regional, and international artists. The Lamasco Microgallery’s mission is rooted in the transformative power of visual experience that adds value to individual and collective perspectives. Additionally, it emphasizes that access to the fine arts can help people grow into more thoughtful and empathetic community citizens.

Stop by when you are walking about for an art and trinket exchange, and to see what is featured in the art gallery at The Perch!

Image Description:

The image showcases a custom-built, miniature wooden display box attached to a metal fence post along a gravel driveway. The installation functions as a whimsical neighborhood micro-art gallery or small curio exchange. Structure & Architecture: The structure is designed to look like a small house, painted dark gray with a gabled roof. The front face features two distinct glass-windowed compartments stacked vertically. Top Compartment: This upper section has a clear window revealing a miniature interior lined with vertical blue-and-white striped wallpaper. Inside, a tiny glass prism or crystal wind chime hangs from the ceiling, alongside a small, framed portrait painting of a terrier dog and a dark green mineral specimen displayed on a wooden stand. Bottom Compartment: The larger lower section features a door crafted from an ornate, antique-style gold metallic frame with a decorative crystal-style doorknob on the right side. The interior shares the same striped wallpaper background and holds a white card displaying a black-and-white line drawing of a teacup and saucer, along with other small trinkets, pins, and crystals sitting on the floor.

It opened in February 2024, and is run by artist and illustrator Amy Talbott. The gallery was founded with two goals in mind: 1) to give artists and creators of all ages, abilities, and walks of life an offline space to share their work. 2) to share art with people in everyday life. Artists from preschoolers to professionals are invited to show their work in the gallery, and most of the gallery’s audience consists of dog walkers, exercisers, and families out for a stroll. locationDescription: At the Corner of Buisson St and Ducommun Ave San Diego CA 92122
summary: IG: @freelittleartgalleryuc The UCFlag (University City Free Little Art Gallery) was installed on November 12, 2025
detail:
IG: @freelittleartgalleryuc

The UCFlag (University City Free Little Art Gallery) was installed on November 12, 2025. It’s a small but meaningful space where neighbors can share their creativity, connect through art, and be inspired by one another’s imagination. I was inspired to create this gallery after seeing others like it, and especially after being diagnosed with breast cancer. Building and curating this tiny gallery has been a way for me to stay creative and positive through challenging times — and to invite others to do the same. The UCFlag is about community, expression, and the joy of giving and receiving art.

Image Description: University City's Free Little Art Gallery

summary: IG: @dianarosestudio Little Free Mug Exchange – South Town Arts District The Little Free Mug Exchange is a year-round community art installation located in t...
detail:
IG: @dianarosestudio

Little Free Mug Exchange – South Town Arts District The Little Free Mug Exchange is a year-round community art installation located in the South Town Arts District. The exchange was made by PDX Dinorama and gifted to Diana Rose Studio, a neighborhood community art studio. The structure was painted and installed by Diana Rose Studio in collaboration with the surrounding neighborhood. The Mug Exchange was officially installed on January 16, 2026, and celebrated with a neighborhood hot cocoa party. Designed to encourage generosity, creativity, and connection, the exchange invites community members to take a mug, leave a mug, or simply enjoy the spirit of shared art in everyday life. The Little Free Mug Exchange will operate year-round and will be featured annually as part of the South Town Art Walk, highlighting South Town’s commitment to accessible, joyful, and community-driven art.

locationDescription: On 16th Street between Martin and Quail Avenues, McAllen, TX
summary: Free little native nursery! We started our free little native nursery in 2025 as a way to share native plants with our neighbors
detail: Free little native nursery! We started our free little native nursery in 2025 as a way to share native plants with our neighbors. We installed a native garden in our backyard and noticed a lot of the plats propagated, but we couldn’t keep them in the garden because they didn’t have room to grow. Instead of removing and discarding the plants, we decided to pot them and give them away for free! I’m out front yard, there is a wooden pallet where we put the potted plants. People are able to just come pick up a plant at their convenience. It’s a way to share the wealth of the garden and to cultivate native plants in our neighborhood to create spaces for local wildlife to flourish. We try to have plants year around but the summer months are harder because of the extreme heat.

detail:
Instagram: @lilgreenartbox

The lilgreenartbox is a community art exchange box between artists young and old. Many of our local small business participate and bring their products to give back to the community. I started our box last July and has just exploded into an amazing thing and never expected the feedback from it. I wanted to do something fun and with myself having a small business I wanted to give back and do something fun! We have two boxes right now, the lilgreenartbox is for trading art and the pink box changes here and there. We’ve done a Small Business Highlight showcasing the talent in our our town! The small businesses that participate bring items to the pink box for patrons to take and don’t have to bring anything in return. It’s more to bring them more followers and for people to find out about their small business. We’ve done a trinket trade and a Christmas ornament exchange as well! Lots more ideas to come! If you take something from the box, please bring something in return so the next people to come aren’t disappointed:)

summary: Instagram: @519TrinketTrade TikTok: @519TrinketTrade Welcome to 519 Trinket Trade — the first of its kind in Forest City, London, Ontario 💕✨ A tiny sidewalk...
detail:
Instagram: @519TrinketTrade

TikTok: @519TrinketTrade

Welcome to 519 Trinket Trade — the first of its kind in Forest City, London, Ontario 💕✨ A tiny sidewalk treasure world where forgotten things get a second main character moment. This whimsical community trinket exchange invites kids, adults, and kids-at-heart to rediscover the magic of giving and finding tiny treasures. Think nostalgic toys, vintage trinkets, cute buttons, fun stickers, and sweet little surprises — all waiting to be loved again. It’s like a treasure hunt… without the hunt. Open the box, discover hidden gems, and trade something of your own to keep the joy going. Give life to your old beloved items and watch them become someone else’s favorite find. Whether it’s a Polly Pocket, a handful of stickers, or a tiny keepsake, every trade spreads happiness, creativity, and connection throughout the neighborhood. Built to spark joy, inspire nostalgia, and remind us of the little things that matter, 519 Trinket Trade is all about slowing down, sharing smiles, and being a kid again 💌 Take a trinket. Leave a trinket. Spread joy — one tiny treasure at a time 💖

704TrinketBox is a mother-daughter project in Charlotte, NC, created from a love of collecting, crafting, nostalgia, and sharing trinkets with others. Located beneath our year-round 12-foot skeleton and watched over by one of our gargoyles, our community trinket exchange is filled with a rotating mix of knick-knacks, small toys, stickers, cards, zines, and other fun finds. The idea is simple: leave a trinket, take a trinket, and help keep the exchange going for the next visitor.

detail:
(currently down, see social media for updates)

*SEASONAL* Will be out December 5th - April 5th

IG: @aztrinketchest

Our installation is called 'AZ Trinket Chest,' inspired by the concept of a treasure chest where you're meant to find esoteric, one-of-a-kind memorabilia.

However, our direct influence came from the Phoenix Trinket Trade installation, which we had the opportunity to visit. The idea of community, togetherness, and reframing the concept of "losing" to "giving" pushed us to open our open box on December 6, 2025.

If there's anything we'd like the community to know when visiting, it's that y'all are welcome any time, any day, however many times you are called to it. Why? Because these installments will always be for the community, by the community.

Instagram: @beavertondowntownassociation

Facebook: @downtownbeaverton

Long before Downtown Beaverton became the vibrant, creative, food-filled community it is today, there was a curious little beaver named Beverly. Legend says Beverly wandered into downtown looking for the perfect place to build her lodge. Instead, she found something even better: amazing small businesses, kind people, hidden art, sweet treats, live music, and tiny moments of magic tucked into every corner. Beverly quickly became obsessed with collecting tiny treasures, shiny trinkets, doodads, and meaningful little objects left behind by the community. Rather than keeping them all to herself, she decided to hide them throughout Downtown Beaverton for others to discover. Now, Beverly spends her days sneaking around downtown, visiting local businesses, sipping boba, sharing pastries, listening to music at the Commons, and expanding her famous Trinket Trail. The Beverly the Beaver Trinket Trail is a community treasure hunt featuring tiny trinket exchange spots hidden throughout Downtown Beaverton. Visitors are encouraged to explore downtown, discover local businesses, take a trinket, leave one behind if they’d like, and help keep Beverly’s adventures going. Because according to Beverly, the best communities are built one tiny treasure, one small business, and one shared moment at a time.

The owner of this spot is the creator or Bloomology, a non profit organization that does drives for supplies and craft classes via the public and in the local domestic violence shelters for adults and children residing. The creator of bloomology is a domestic violence survivor who went into the domestic violence shelter with three kids but has since graduated, became a surrogate, started Bloomology, and continues a movement full of joy and healthy healing. The little free library we created was meant to be an interactive experience where you can do the traditional exchanging of books but also enjoy the artwork and the free little art gallery where we share art that we make at home amongst our healing journey, make a wish in the wishing well, and take an art kit to create something of your own to spread the joy of creativity.

detail:
Instagram: @brewerytowntrinkets

Located at the highly visible corner of 28th Street and Girard Avenue in Brewerytown, the Brewerytown Trinket Box is a colorful community art installation that transforms an ordinary utility box into a small-scale public art piece. The project celebrates the neighborhood’s creativity and history while adding character to one of Brewerytown’s main commercial corridors, helping make the intersection more welcoming and pedestrian-friendly. Situated near historic brewery-era architecture and ongoing neighborhood revitalization efforts, it serves as a reminder that even small interventions can contribute to a stronger sense of place.

Image Description:

Mounted to a utility pole at the corner of 28th and Girard, the Brewerytown Trinket Box is a tiny slice of neighborhood magic hidden in plain sight. Surrounded by classic Philly rowhomes, busy sidewalks, and the daily comings and goings of Brewerytown residents, it invites neighbors to take one trinket, leave one trinket, and be part of a shared community story. Equal parts public art project and block-corner conversation starter, it’s the kind of small, unexpected delight that gives Philadelphia neighborhoods their unmistakable character.

We are also looking for artists and orgs to be added / donate and feature them on our socials!

A junction box, with a double latch and pull tab that is accessible by ramp and stairs. There is a sign that says NYC Trinket Trade on the box. The purpose is to take a trinket, and leave a trinket.

name: Carson’s Trinket Box
locationDescription: E 169th St & Avalon Blvd, Carson, CA 90746
summary: TikTok: @poohskeeper I created Carson’s Trinket Box in early April to give my community a space to showcase their cherished items and artwork
detail:
TikTok: @poohskeeper

I created Carson’s Trinket Box in early April to give my community a space to showcase their cherished items and artwork. I was inspired by the joy I saw on TikTok, and since then, I’ve watched both kids and adults light up when they find something they’ve been hoping for, all thanks to a TikTok inventory post. My only ask is to treat the box with care: no stealing, and take as many trinkets as you’d like. Let’s spread happiness together!

Image Description:

On the table, there is a decorated pink box labeled “TRINKET trade BOX!” in handwritten text, surrounded by colorful cartoon stickers. The top of the box has additional handwritten notes: * “PLEASE DO NOT STEAL” * “Take A Trinket, Leave 1” (with small drawings and more stickers) Next to the box, there’s a small metal basket containing various small toys and trinkets. In front of the basket, a slightly crumpled piece of paper is taped to the table with a handwritten sign: TRINKET TRADE BOX EXCESS BIN! Place anything that can not fit inside the box inside here! Thank you! Happy trading!!

summary: TikTok: @divine.little.tri ✨ Divine Little Trinkets ✨ Located at Sissy’s Tacos in Mount Washington 40047, this Community Trinket Trading Box was created with...
detail:
TikTok: @divine.little.tri

✨ Divine Little Trinkets ✨ Located at Sissy’s Tacos in Mount Washington 40047, this Community Trinket Trading Box was created with a purpose far greater than simply trading small treasures. It represents community, connection, hope, and the reminder that even in a world that can sometimes feel heavy and dark, there is still light to be found. It is a place meant to inspire people of all ages young and old alike to believe that healing is possible, kindness still exists, and no one has to walk through difficult seasons alone. Every trinket placed inside carries a story, a memory, a little piece of joy passed from one person to another. A reminder that even the smallest things can make the biggest difference in someone’s day. May this little box serve as a symbol of strength, resilience, and new beginnings proof that no matter how dark life may seem, there is always light at the end of the tunnel, and you are capable of finding your way back to it. ✨ Opening June 2026. 🤍

name: Five.ohfinds Trinket Trade Box
summary: Instagram & TikTok: @five.ohfinds Five.ohfinds trinket trade box The Trinket Trade Box was created in 2026 in Mesquite, Texas as a small community space wher...
detail:
Instagram & TikTok: @five.ohfinds

Five.ohfinds trinket trade box The Trinket Trade Box was created in 2026 in Mesquite, Texas as a small community space where people can share and exchange cute trinkets with one another. The idea was inspired by the love for collecting little treasures and the joy that comes from trading and discovering something new. This space was built with the intention of bringing the local community together in a fun and friendly way. Visitors are encouraged to follow the simple idea of “take one, leave one” so that everyone has the chance to enjoy the experience. When people stop by, I hope they feel a little bit of excitement and nostalgia — like finding a tiny treasure. The goal is to keep the magic going by being kind, respectful, and leaving something for the next person to discover.

This image shows a small, charming trinket trade box mounted on a wooden post in front of a cozy, cottage-style bookstore. The box itself is rectangular and painted a soft, muted green. It has a simple front door with a latch and is decorated with hand-painted details. At the top, it reads “Gloucester Trinket Trade” in neat lettering. Near the bottom, there are small, bright yellow flower illustrations, adding a cheerful, handmade feel. Beneath the flowers, the phrase “Take one, leave one” is written, inviting people to participate in the exchange. The box is attached to a tall, natural wood post positioned just off a white-painted ramp leading up to the building. Behind it sits a pale yellow, two-story structure with white trim and a welcoming red front door. A white railing lines the ramp and steps, giving the space an accessible, friendly appearance.

Facebook: Homosassa Trinket Trade Box

Open every Saturday and Sunday from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. .

My spot is is located on the front porch of my store, Willow Moon Mystical inside of Howard's Flea Market in Homosassa Florida. I began the Homosassa trinket Trade Center as I seen they started popping up in Florida and I wanted our little county to be included. I think they are a wonderful idea for promoting community unity, a great way to visit memory Lane, and also to create new memories. The Homosassa trinket Trade Center box is open every Saturday and Sunday from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. . Come trade with us.

Image Description:

Mounted on the wall in front of Willow Moon Mystical inside Howard’s Flea Market in Building ED9, this brightly decorated Homosassa Trinket Trade Center box invites visitors to take part in a little local magic. Although four different businesses share the same building, each has its own separate entrance, and this box marks the front of your shop with color and charm. The box is covered in playful, multicolored letters that read: HOMOSASSA TRINKET TRADE CENTER TAKE ONE LEAVE ONE NO FOOD PLEASE The surface is adorned with cheerful stickers — butterflies, flowers, a mushroom, and sparkling gem accents — giving it a whimsical, welcoming feel. Crocheted yarn pieces and beaded decorations frame the edges, adding a handmade, heartfelt touch. Inside the open compartments are tiny treasures waiting to be traded: a blue rubber duck, a plush pink heart, a tiny gray mouse toy, colorful beads, charms, stickers, and other small delights. Each section holds a different surprise, inviting visitors to explore, exchange, and share. The overall look is vibrant, inviting, and full of community spirit — a Homosassa original that brings joy to everyone who passes by your storefront.

The new version of the trinket box is a tall cabinet located next to the snack counter. detail:
Facebook: NaTaco Norman

Welcome to Let’s Taco ‘Bout Trinkets! 🌮✨ I started this little spot to bring some joy, connection, and a sprinkle of surprise to our community. Feel free to take a trinket, leave a trinket, or just stop by and smile! Bonus love if you add a taco-themed treasure! 💛

Image Description:

A small, house-shaped wooden Little Free Library stands outdoors on a concrete base, surrounded by green grass and tall evergreen trees. The structure has a peaked roof with a black lantern-style light mounted at the top. On the front are two doors with black hinges—an upper compartment with a small square window framed in bright yellow, and a larger lower door. A sign on the front reads “Free Little Library” with colorful books illustrated beneath it. To the right side hangs a bright yellow fabric bag with a book-themed design and a quote about reading. A small doorbell-style camera and a “Security Notice” sign are also mounted near the upper door. The overall scene feels peaceful, inviting, and community-centered.

name: Lil Fairy Trinket Post
summary: Did you read the Borrowers as a kid? Have you ever imagined what a gnome, elf, or anthropomorphic toad would keep in it's secret stash? Our little trinket tr...
detail:
Did you read the Borrowers as a kid? Have you ever imagined what a gnome, elf, or anthropomorphic toad would keep in it's secret stash? Our little trinket trafe is dedicated to the humble little doodad that might be scrounged from the back of the junk drawer, the bottom of the toy box or the recesses of your craft hoard, but is still delightful and cute nonetheless. A small box within our little free library with little compartments, so only trinkets around 2" or less will fit.

We welcome handmade items, and often include little handmade patches or pins or little craft supplies.

Take one, help restock the whimsy if you can. Thanks!

My dream of having a LFL of my very own came true in July 2024! I opened Little Unicorn Library book box for kids. There is also a painted rock garden and many fiction place signs along the fence! I always had imagined having 2 boxes and in August 2024 I opened my Little Unicorn’s Glimmers of Joy kindness box. There I have books for teens and adults. I also have space for bigger items and kindness gifts.. because this space is always evolving, in February 2025 I added Little Unicorn’s Keychain and Trinket Exchange (inspired by Mike Bennett)!

✅ Keychains ✅ Charms ✅ Stickers ✅ Mini toys ✅ Figurines ✅ Handmade goodies ✅ Small cute or spooky treasures

📍 WHERE CAN YOU FIND US? Lulu’s Trinket Lockers are part of the Worldwide Sidewalk Joy community! 🌎✨ 🗺️ Find us on the Sidewalk Joy Map: https://worldwidesidewalkjoy.com/the-map 🎥 Follow us on TikTok @lalachicagolove for locker restocks, new trinkets, trades and behind-the-scenes fun! 🎀🎃 We hope Lulu’s Trinket Lockers bring a little JOY, MAGIC & SURPRISE to our community! 🥹💕 ✨ Come find a trinket. name: Missoula Trinket Trade
locationDescription: Home ReSource located at 1515 Wyoming St, Missoula MT 59801
summary: Instagram: @missoulatrinkettrade Missoula Trinket Trade 🌸 I was inspired by Trinket Trades across the country through Instagram while I was living in Seattle...
detail:
Instagram: @missoulatrinkettrade

Missoula Trinket Trade 🌸 I was inspired by Trinket Trades across the country through Instagram while I was living in Seattle while my fiancé had to undergo a thymectomy, chemotherapy and a bone marrow transplant. We were there for 6 months, and all I wanted was to make him happy, which turned into wanting that for the community that supported him. I want people to have something fun, engaging and just a break from anything painful, stressful, etc- its so easy to cloud your vision when you feel like that. I want that fog to break when they open the trinket box. I really do.

name: Peace, Love & Trinkets
summary: TikTok: @@localbushbabe Howdy Yall, I’m Tara 🫶🏽 I am new to the trinket trading world but about 2 months ago my granddaughters friend was diagnosed with cancer
detail:
TikTok: @@localbushbabe

Howdy Yall, I’m Tara 🫶🏽 I am new to the trinket trading world but about 2 months ago my granddaughters friend was diagnosed with cancer. At 10 years old. Broke my heart. They wanted to sell there toys to help her family pay for medical things. But I suggested to them to focus on there friend and making her smile everyday. Then I saw a trinket box on TikTok for the first time. I had to do it, for them, for her. For all souls who just need something to feel alive and smile again. And what started out as a very small trinket box very quickly grew into very Texas sized box. I am the only one in my town at the moment who has one so it’s kind of special to us. Can I love all those visitors and their friend comes by quite often to see what everyone has left to trade so it’s purpose has been filled.

Image Description:

It’s a big ol Texas size box with some groovy painting and a window style door

summary: 34-06 73rd St, Jackson Heights, NY 11372 **Check hours before visiting** IG: @nyctrinkettrade We established @nyctrinkettrade to create joy and community thr...
detail:
34-06 73rd St, Jackson Heights, NY 11372

**Check hours before visiting**

IG: @nyctrinkettrade

We established @nyctrinkettrade to create joy and community through trinket swapping. This is one box of 5 throughout New York City (1 in each borough). Everyone is welcome, rain or shine, to take a trinket, leave a trinket. The box is accessible via ramp or stairs. We are also looking for artists and orgs to be added / donate and feature them on our socials! Image Description: A junction box, with a double latch and pull tab that is accessible by ramp and stairs. There is a sign that says NYC Trinket Trade on the box. The box is installed on a rail in front of the The World's Borough Bookshop in Queens. When you open the box there are lots of trinkets (stickers, prints, keychains etc). The purpose is to take a trinket, and leave a trinket. The store hours are M-F 12 pm to 7pm and weekends from 11am to 8pm.

Hi! I’m Lakota, the creator behind a community trinket trade box in Quincy built to spread kindness, creativity, and connection one tiny treasure at a time. What started as a small idea on my property has grown into a space where neighbors of all ages can leave art, toys, crafts, notes, and little surprises for others to discover. My goal is simple: create a little pocket of joy where people feel welcome, inspired, and connected to their community. Whether someone stops by to trade, donate, or simply smile at what they find, every interaction helps keep the magic going. Around here, even the smallest trinket can make someone’s day a little brighter

Their love of nature, history, vintage items, and all things whimsical has turned into this passion project that they hope you can be a part of! 🩷

Image Description:

This fairy garden inspired box is covered in moss and dried hydrangeas with twig stumps on the sides. The box itself is a muted green with glass on both the sides and front door. It is placed on a wood pole and is in the middle of a garden with a white fence, lilly of the valley flowers, a cherry blossom tree, and a porch in the background. There are several trinkets inside such as sunflower seed packets, gold rings, photos of the beach, small glass jars filled with seashells, a marble ball, a flower hair clip, a mini clay pot, a mug with small quotes, a watch, a candle, & wooden dolphin figurine.

detail: The 44th Street Treasure House is a repurposed dollhouse with a big heart. This treasure library invites neighbors of all ages to open a door, find a treasure, and leave a bit of magic behind. Find a treasure you love? Take it! Have something you don’t need anymore? Leave it to become someone else’s joy! The treasure house was created for a neighborhood-wide Wonder Week in August 2025. While our great neighborhood has plenty of little libraries, nothing felt as if it catered to kids- and kids at heart! Anything left in front of the house, or hanging on the side hooks, is fair game to take home. Our goal is to spread joy- one treasure at a time! 🧡

name: The Crow’s Curiosities Trinket Box
summary: TikTok: @casa.mapache This trinket box is located in a book inside the Casa Mapache library! We love a good trinket, including things that are truly weird an...
detail:
TikTok: @casa.mapache

This trinket box is located in a book inside the Casa Mapache library! We love a good trinket, including things that are truly weird and wonderful, so bring your curios to trade—toys, antiques, even a good crystal are all welcomed! That said, it is a relatively small box for the time being. We will expand if it works well! A family of raccoons, mapache in Spanish, love to use our evergreen trees to climb to their nightly excursions. We also get javelinas, rabbits, hawks, roadrunners, and even an occasional coyote in our neighborhood! That’s where the name of our library comes from! After years of wanting a free library of our own, we decided to build one! We have plenty of loved books from our own library as well as a number graciously donated by the Friends of the Pima County Public Library. Come take a book to enjoy while you’re reading trinkets, and if you have a title to leave we’d love to share it!

name: The Spectrum Trinket Trade & Puzzle Swap
summary: Meet The Spectrum Trinket Trade infront of @haus2muc at @kreativquartier_muenchen ! It's a micro-sociological art intervention in the public space
detail: Meet The Spectrum Trinket Trade infront of @haus2muc at @kreativquartier_muenchen ! It's a micro-sociological art intervention in the public space. In a city like Munich, it challenges wealth inequality by completely removing material value from the equation. Swap, share, and connect away from consumer culture. A Trinket Trade is all about swapping small, quirky, and fun little treasures (think stickers, cool buttons, tiny figurines, handmade bracelets, or that cool rock you found). It’s not about value; it’s about sharing a smile and a story. 📍 Outside Haus2 | Always Free Schwere-Reiter-Str.2B, Munich

The Shepherd Street Little Free Library and Trinket Trading Post are community spaces created to encourage sharing, curiosity, and connection. Visitors are invited to borrow or leave a book, trade a small treasure, and enjoy the simple joy of giving and discovering something new. Together, they bring neighbours of all ages together through kindness, creativity, and a love of community.

Image Description:

The Shepherd Street Little Free Library is a small, freestanding wooden library located near the sidewalk. It resembles a miniature house with a front door that opens to shelves filled with books for readers of all ages. Visitors are welcome to take a book, leave a book, or simply browse the collection at any time. Beside the library is the Trinket Trading Post, a matching wooden cabinet filled with small treasures such as keychains, figurines, polished stones, stickers, toys, and other tiny keepsakes. The idea is simple: take a trinket you love and, if you can, leave another small treasure for someone else to discover. Both spaces are designed to be welcoming, accessible, and community-driven, creating moments of surprise, generosity, and connection for neighbours of all ages.

Image Description:

A large tree stands beside a residential street at dusk. Attached to the tree trunk is a small, rectangular pink plastic box that resembles a waterproof storage case. The front of the box has been decorated by hand with glitter, rhinestones and pastel artwork in pink, lavender, turquoise, white and silver. At the top, a turquoise panel reads "Tiny Treasures" in black handwritten letters. Below are several whimsical glitter covered shapes, including hearts, abstract blobs, a palm tree all to look like a treasure map with a treasure chest. Along the bottom, another turquoise panel reads "Trinket Trade" in playful letters. A decorative green vine wrap around the tree. In the background are a quiet neighborhood street, a small white house, trimmed hedges, overhead utility lines, and part of a red vehicle parked at the curb. The overall scene suggests a community "tiny treasure" box where passersby are invited to take a small trinket or surprise.

summary: TikTok & Instagram: @tbtrinketbox Tobby & Baji’s Trinket Box 🐾 This small community installation was created to bring a little joy and connection into our ne...
detail:
TikTok & Instagram: @tbtrinketbox

Tobby & Baji’s Trinket Box 🐾 This small community installation was created to bring a little joy and connection into our neighborhood through the exchange of tiny treasures. Inspired by the idea that even the smallest items can spark happiness, the Trinket Box invites visitors to take a trinket, leave a trinket, and share in a moment of curiosity and kindness. I noticed that Manteca doesn’t currently have a trinket exchange like this, and I wanted to create something special for our little town—a simple, welcoming space that encourages creativity, generosity, and connection. Named after my two dogs, Tobby and Baji—our “paw-fficial” treasure inspectors—this space reflects their playful spirit and love for discovery. The box was built in 2026 as a creative, low-cost way to bring something unique to the community. When you stop by, I hope you feel welcome to explore, trade something meaningful, and leave with a smile. Whether you’re leaving a charm, sticker, or small surprise, you’re contributing to a shared experience rooted in joy and kindness.

Image Description:

A small, handmade outdoor “little free library”-style box stands on a wooden post in a yard. The box is open at the front and painted white inside with purple trim along the edges. The roof is decorated with a colorful mosaic made of broken tiles and pottery pieces in many shapes and colors—blues, reds, greens, and some with patterns like rainbows and swirls. Inside, there are two wooden shelves filled with small toys and trinkets. On the top shelf, there is a shallow black pan holding small balls and plastic items. Next to it are a baseball, a small Santa figurine, a gray elephant toy, and a purple pig-shaped object. A small stuffed animal sits toward the back. On the bottom shelf, there are more toys and playful objects: small toy cars, a plush chick, a pink stuffed creature, colorful beads in a clear plastic drawer organizer, bright blue sunglasses, and a few pens or markers. Some items are loosely scattered, giving it a casual, shared feel. The box is outdoors, with dry grass and a house visible in the background. The overall scene feels like a neighborhood sharing spot where people leave and take small toys or treasures.

detail:
Instagram: @tinyswapws

The West Salem Tiny Swap Museum is here to connect community, spark joy, encourage creativity, and build a tiny alternative economy. We love toys and trinkets, fidgets and findings, and especially handmade art, and we curate the Tiny Swap to be and inclusive and LGBTQ+ friendly site of whimsy and sharing in a historic neighborhood and across from a church that does a ton for the community. We ask visitors to be mindful of balancing what they take and what they bring, even if it’s not on the same day; don’t miss the duck trade and mug swap, but please just admire (and don’t walk off with) other yard decor.

Image Description:

summary: Instagram : @ConeysCorner “Coney’s Corner Community Dog Lovers’ Exchange of Crystal Beach” is Sidewalk Joy for All Dogs & their Kind Humans
detail:
Instagram : @ConeysCorner

“Coney’s Corner Community Dog Lovers’ Exchange of Crystal Beach” is Sidewalk Joy for All Dogs & their Kind Humans. Coney's Corner came to be from a genuine, heartfelt inspiration to add a glimmer of joy and caring connection in an ever-challenging world. The heart of Coney's Corner Community Dog Lovers' Exchange comes from the kind neighbors, visitors & passers-by who walk their sweetie dogs in dog-friendly Crystal Beach, FL every day. Each dog breaks the ice for their kind humans to say "Hello" and wish each other a good day, hopefully carrying that goodness back out into the world. After discovering #SidewalkJoy on Instagram @pdxdinorama - and then @luckydoglibrary in Portland - we just knew that theme would be a perfect fit for our little community! Maybe there could be a way to help add a little joy to the day, smiles to faces, and bring community together (and also help others if they have needs for their dogs) ... "Coney's Corner" was born : 14Feb2026 Need something for your Pup, Please Take! Have Extra Doggy Things to Share, Leave for Others to Enjoy! How Cool when Neighbors Become Friends, when Friends Create Community, when Community provides Connection, Caring, and Value – Together, We All Make the World a Little Bit Brighter... ... All Starting with the Gentle Offerings of One Dog and One Human.

Image Description:

Spread the LOVE: Use #ConeysCorner on Instagram and tag @ConeysCorner to spread some love with pics of your sweetie dog enjoying & sharing fun things with Coney’s Corner Community of Crystal Beach! name: Hexenhaus Zauberkasten (Witches' House Magic Box)
summary: This little house is inspired by and painted after my Omi's (grandmother's) house in a small town in Austria
detail:
This little house is inspired by and painted after my Omi's (grandmother's) house in a small town in Austria. My Omi is the most hardworking, generous and caring person I know. She has spent her entire life providing for her family and the larger community through the harvest of her impressive garden and acts of kindness like creating crafts to support the Red Cross. I wanted to continue the spirit of home, generosity and community that I've always felt at my Omi's house -- here in Vallejo! The Zauberkasten is a work in progress. Though fully functional now (full of both trinkets and books), there are plans in the works to add a shelf; lights, and other extensions for trinkets and seeds. Established in 2026, the "Magic Box" has already received generous offerings of trinkets and books. I plan to incorporate a seed library in the near future. Welcome to the Hexenhaus Zauberkasten!

Image Description:

A miniature house on a post in a yard full of bushy flowers and trees. The house is pale green with a dark brown roof and trim. The front door has a clear window with brown trim encircling and crossing it.

Magnolia cottage has a Little Fairy Forest, Built 2021 and still growing. I run Bigfoot Hideaway a BnB and it is nestled in the forest on my property on the way to Bigfoot cabin. They say my property is like walking through an enchanting garden. Part of the them is Bigfoot, if you can count all the bigfoots in and around the property you get a prize. I am in the process of building another nook 3x3 ft before my entrance to my gate. I hope to have it up and ready by March 2026. The one by my gate that will be able to be seen from the road will be year round.

name: Must Love Dogs
locationDescription: SE 66th Ave Between SE Duke & SE Tolmam, Portland, OR, 97206
summary: Instagram: @woofwalkerpdx Nestled just by my home, this unique spot started as a simple dog rest area where furry friends could quench their thirst and enjoy...
detail:
Instagram: @woofwalkerpdx

Nestled just by my home, this unique spot started as a simple dog rest area where furry friends could quench their thirst and enjoy a tasty treat. It quickly blossomed into a vibrant treat station and rock art haven, inviting guests to express their creativity. Visitors are encouraged to paint rocks and inscribe their beloved pets’ names, leaving a trail of colorful memories for others to enjoy. Inspired by my niece’s love for adventure, I introduced a geocache to the station, adding an element of exploration for dog owners and their pups alike. This growing community hub is all about celebrating the joy of dogs, fostering creativity, and building connections among animal lovers.

Image Description:

The image captures a charming dog rest stop situated in front of a home. At the forefront, a white post features a small treat dispenser filled with dog treats, accompanied by a playful sign that humorously questions if dogs ever receive half treats. Nearby, a photo of a dog adds a personal touch. Surrounding the post, colorful painted rocks are scattered across a pebbled area, each inscribed with the names of beloved pets, showcasing the community’s creative spirit. Decorative elements like black cutouts of dogs and whimsical flowers enhance the inviting atmosphere. A water bowl is positioned nearby, ensuring that furry visitors can stay hydrated. The entire setup exudes warmth and a love for dogs, making it a delightful stop for both pets and their owners.

name: Phantom Curiosities
summary: IG: @PhantomCuriosities Phantom Curiosities is a little free curio created in the spirit of The Phantom Tollbooth
detail:
IG: @PhantomCuriosities

Phantom Curiosities is a little free curio created in the spirit of The Phantom Tollbooth. Mysterious and ever changing, it’s a place where anything is possible. Inside the cabinet, you might find fortunes waiting to be revealed, tiny figures and animals seeking new homes, stickers to collect, pins to trade, or even a few treats for passing dogs. Each visit brings something different… Sometimes sweet, sometimes strange, always a little magical. Nearby is Totoro’s Garden, a spiral portal installation to leave pennies and other small tokens for the neighborhood guardians (who, if you look carefully, you might find hidden among the leaves). locationDescription: 939 Dudley Avenue (between Harrow Street and Guelph Street) in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada.
summary: IG: @roostertownpoetry Rooster Town Poetry Shed is a streetside poetry box displaying rousing and inspiring poems from Canada and around the world
detail:
IG: @roostertownpoetry

Rooster Town Poetry Shed is a streetside poetry box displaying rousing and inspiring poems from Canada and around the world. It launched in 2025 with a visual poetry installation by Jennifer Still, Winnipeg's Poet Laureate. The shed is a rooster's crow away from the final site of Rooster Town, where a vibrant community of Métis families were heartlessly forced from their homes in the 1950s to make way for urban development. The shed honours their memory.

The shed is situated on Treaty 1 Territory, the ancestral lands of the Anishinaabeg, Anishininewuk, Dakota Oyate, Denesuline, and Nehethowuk Nations. It also sits on the Homeland of the Red River Métis.

Open to all ages, abilities, and backgrounds, this special corner invites visitors to swap more than just books. Founded by Rowena Cage, an artist, author, and advocate, the Bliss Exchange offers a delightful mix of items to share and enjoy. Alongside books, you’ll discover a rotated Lego Exchange, Love Note Exchange, Mini Car Exchange, Bugs and Crawler Exchange and even a Free Period Products Exchange, thanks to a partnership with local nonprofit Access Period. The idea for the street jar collective was born out of learning an astonishing fact: Every year, Australians use over 1.3 million tonnes of glass packaging, and less than half is recycled. It turns out, a lot of people don't like throwing out their glass jars, with many quietly admitting they are jar hoarders - if only they had a way to share them for reuse! Borrowing a book title for each street jar library is a way to capture people's imagination and hopefully prompt them to set up their own jar library.

detail:
Instagram: @renee.poetry.fence

Since 2009, I've had a 93-foot "Poetry Fence" next to my house, outdoors, year-round, 24/7. 17 years. Curated entirely by me, Renee Adams, with first Little Free Library in Northern Virginia. People come to read poetry, get inspiration, occasional long articles, find comfort. They read quietly, bring friends and family visiting from other cities or countries, or reach out to me in my garden to talk. I often invite kids and adults to come inside the enclosure to see fairy gardens. People leave comments on the fence bulletin board saying how much it's meant to them. Kids grew up with the fence for 17 years, telling me it got them started writing poetry or "getting up" (in the science area) "on the fence was better than winning the $250,000 high school science research prize" for best in entire nation. People take poems from the poetry mailbox. Toddlers play with treasures in the fence window and see the pond and creatures in my garden. One teenager brought kids he was babysitting to play in the window and said it was a "community stopping place," and his parents read him poetry as a kid, as many other parents have. Come by and experience it yourself!

The stone sculptures are created right here at Sticks and Stones Farm, using found stone gathered locally and shaped slowly by hand. Influenced by the land, the rhythm of family life, and the joy of building alongside kids and animals, each piece carries a sense of warmth, whimsy, and groundedness. These sculptures are made to be touched, climbed on, wondered about, and lived with.

name: The BirdCalls! Project Phone
locationDescription: Flower Avenue and Erie Avenue, in front of Mansa Kunda Restaurant, Takoma Park, MD 20912
summary: IG: @quietlifemotel The BirdCalls! project hotwires derelict payphones for ornithological purposes
detail:
IG: @quietlifemotel

The BirdCalls! project hotwires derelict payphones for ornithological purposes. The original BirdCalls! phone is a public art project created for Takoma Park by David Schulman in 2016, with engineering by Branden Hall. The phone uses field recordings from the Cornell Lab of Ornithology to feature the sounds of local birds. Voices of a few public radio peeps also found their way into this trilingual phone, somehow ... 411! 411! Subsequent BirdCalls! phones are roosting (or roosting soon) in Culver City, CA, and McMinnville, OR.

detail:

The Connection Desk is a community-rooted art installation in Winnipeg’s Luxton/North End neighbourhood, created by Gillian Crawford in memory of her father. Featuring a vintage desk and a disconnected rotary phone, it invites visitors to sit, speak to someone they’ve lost, and connect with their memories. What began as a personal expression of grief has grown into a shared space of remembrance and quiet connection within the community.

detail:
www.fairypenpals.com

The Fairy Tree garden was on the Kelly Clarkson Show twice. It began during the pandemic as a place where children could write to fairies and get letters back. The whole community joined to create a fairy garden that lights up at night and changes often with new installations ranging from hypertufa troll heads to a Geo Cache, Tooth Fairy and even the Humble Bees and their Queen, Bee-yoncé. People of all ages come to share their joys and sorrows with magical beings who heer, advise and support them with over 8,000 letters answered and counting! There is also a Little Free Library and Wishing Well. Displays are constantly changing it is evolving year-round.

summary: IG: @TheGateGuySF. "The Gate Project" is an installation art piece that blends art with craft by using strips of recycled plastic tablecloths to create image...
detail:
IG: @TheGateGuySF.

"The Gate Project" is an installation art piece that blends art with craft by using strips of recycled plastic tablecloths to create images that range from old masters to cartoons and everything in between. Started in 2014 as a way to have images for a calendar for his mother, has evolved into a city wide favorite that changes every single month. Each installation take upwards of 40 hours and only lasts about three weeks before it's taken down and a new one starts at the beginning of each month. Stop by the first week of each month and you may catch him working. Past installations can be found on his Instagram account @TheGateGuySF.

detail:
SEASONAL: Open Nov 1 - Jan 1

#vistawishingtree

The Vista Wishing Tree is a neighborhood tradition where all are invited to write their wishes, hopes, or intentions on a tag and attaches it to a tree. The Wishing Tree Process * Make a wish: Think of a hope, an intention, or a dream you have. * Write or create your offering: Refect and write your wish on a tag. * Attach the offering: Securely tie or hang your wish onto the Wishing Tree. * Leave it to be carried: The belief is that the wind will carry the wish away, a symbolic act that sets your intention in motion. Vista Wishing Tree is up annually Nov 1 - Jan 1.
